specName: Glob spec directories list the specs inside them

spec: Write every scenario as WHEN/THEN with exactly one observable outcome
Reserve backticks for real identifiers a reader would copy, never ordinary nouns
plan: Name the capability each decision belongs to, so the fold knows where it goes
Prefer extending the file that already owns a concern over adding a new one

core-spec-discovery: Spec locations are configured, not assumed
Spec discovery and file-to-spec attribution agree
Reference material declared by a workflow is never mistaken for a spec
The extension notices spec changes wherever specs live
The completion of the implement step is closed by observing the work, not by trusting a report

FR-001.title: A glob match holding its own markdown or spec context is one spec
tests: src/core/specDirectoryResolver.test.ts::leaves an OpenSpec archive folder unexpanded under a wildcard-ending glob

FR-002.title: A glob match holding neither is a container: its content-bearing subfolders are listed, else nothing
tests: src/core/specDirectoryResolver.test.ts::lists the spec folders inside each match
lists nothing for a folder of specs that holds no spec yet

FR-003.title: File attribution returns the same spec folder discovery lists
tests: src/core/specDirectoryResolver.test.ts::attributes a file to the spec folder inside a glob ending in a plain name

FR-004.title: Globs that already match spec folders keep producing the same specs

FR-005.title: A spec reached through several patterns is listed once

tests: src/core/specDirectoryResolver.test.ts::does not treat a project holding a folder of specs as a change root
returns the change folder above a specs segment

expectations: Searching more than one level below a container
context: area: src/core/specDirectoryResolver.ts (glob expansion and file-to-spec attribution)
constraint: plain names and globs share one content test
intent: A glob in speckit.specDirectories that matches a folder of specs lists the specs inside, not the folder
approach: Treat a glob match without its own markdown or spec context as a container and list its content-bearing subfolders, in discovery and attribution alike

T001.did: Shared own-content test; glob deep pass steps into containers; fallback requires content

T002.did: Attribution steps one level below a contentless glob match

T003.did: Container layout, empty container, attribution through a container; 3 new tests fail on main

T004.did: Setting description, configuration doc and changelog say a contentless match is a folder of specs

verified.result: Snapshots:   0 total · Time:        1.219 s · Ran all test suites matching /src\/core\/specDirectoryResolver.test.ts/i.

decisions.decision: A glob match is a container only when it holds no markdown and no spec context of its own
decisions.why: the same content test plain names use, so OpenSpec change folders holding proposal.md stay specs
decisions.rejected: requiring a spec file, which hides every OpenSpec change

decisions.why: isInsideSpecDirectory is synchronous and called from watchers
decisions.rejected: making attribution async across every caller

decisions.decision: Read a glob ending in a plain name as that pattern plus /* instead of judging each match by its content
decisions.why: review round one found the content rule expanded the OpenSpec archive folder and let discovery and attribution disagree
decisions.rejected: per-match disk checks for container vs spec

decisions.decision: A change root must hold proposal.md
decisions.why: otherwise a monorepo project folder is walked, node_modules included, for related docs

decisions.decision: Change roots are skipped only for rewritten plain-name globs, not gated on proposal.md
decisions.why: round two found the proposal.md gate broke non-OpenSpec two-level layouts like features/*/specs/*

decisions.decision: A glob ending in a plain name always means a folder of specs, and the dead fallback is deleted
decisions.why: one reading, matching plain names; configs that relied on the old reading add /*
decisions.rejected: keeping a per-match disk check to guess the meaning

concerns.note: A container holding a stray README.md still reads as one spec; a stricter content test would fix it and is out of scope
